title: A graded cohomological boundary-module criterion for uniform Mittag-Leffler stabilization

standard_prerequisites.name: Sheaf cohomology long exact sequence and naturality
standard_prerequisites.statement: A short exact sequence induces connecting maps natural in a commutative diagram.

standard_prerequisites.name: Noetherian graded modules
standard_prerequisites.statement: The ascending chain condition implies a graded submodule has finitely many homogeneous generators.

core_obligations: Construct the graded submodule of connecting-map images by defining lift-then-multiply maps between successive quotient sheaves and checking compatibility.
Use finitely many homogeneous obstruction generators to correct any cohomology class into a lift; show the correction vanishes a uniformly bounded number of stages down and deduce stabilized images.

proof_roadmap.step: Construct and verify the graded obstruction module.
Correct by its finite generators and obtain the uniform stabilization lag.

difficulty_reason: A finite generating set for all cohomological obstructions is converted into a uniform lifting correction across an inverse system. Naturality alone does not produce the correction or its uniform vanishing level.

compared.difference: That later claim identifies limit and I-adic topologies under degree-p ACC; this target proves uniform Mittag-Leffler image stabilization from degree-(p+1) obstruction-module ACC.

dedup.scope: Read first35 lines of54 current public primary excerpts restricted to cohomology/derived source families and matched exact original label; no target hit. Current research main-overlap/index and P prepared scope checked.

editorial_scope: One original lemma with full proof; context makes explicit that the system consists of A/I^n-module sheaves. No I-adic topology claim is added.

preamble_spans.label: native theorem environments and math macros

editorial_notes: The surrounding source explicitly works with inverse systems of A/I^n-modules. The proof uses this when lift-then-multiply is independent of the lift and when a correction vanishes at level n-c.
The degree-zero piece is H^p(X,F_1), and the finite number of initial stages does not affect the Mittag-Leffler conclusion.
